fact_check.claim: Fall 2024 and later: at least 6 courses totaling a minimum of 18 credits
fact_check.note: Page says at least 6 courses totaling a minimum of 18 credits.

fact_check.claim: Courses from at least 3 different groups, including at least 3 credits from Group 7 (RE)
fact_check.note: At least 3 of 7 groups; at least 3 credits from Group 7.

fact_check.claim: At least two courses at the 2000 level or higher; page does not say whether 1000-level counts for the rest
fact_check.note: Matches; the page is silent on 1000-level, as the article says.

fact_check.claim: No more than two Group 6 (CE) courses; CE courses designated by CCGB, no petitions
fact_check.note: Matches, including the 'no petitions' wording.

fact_check.claim: A course with more than one category (e.g. SSC-AS) counts toward only one
fact_check.note: Page: may only be applied towards one of those categories.

fact_check.claim: A course without a designation is approved in the same categories as its cross-listed or combined course
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: The seven group names (Cultural Analysis, Literature and the Arts, and Social Differences; Historical Analysis; Ethics, Cognition, and Moral Reasoning; Social Science and Global Citizenship; Foreign Languages; Communications in Engineering; Race and Equity)
fact_check.note: All seven names and order match.

fact_check.claim: Group 5 (FL) covers courses that teach language skills; literature courses excluded
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: The Fall 2024 page does not say whether AP credit or S/U grades count
fact_check.note: Neither is mentioned on the page.

fact_check.claim: Engineering links a 'Search for Approved Liberal Studies' tool at liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu; requirements differ by entry year with separate policies
fact_check.note: Page mentions the tool and links three entry-year policies (Fall 2024+, Fall 2020-Spring 2024, Fall 2019 and earlier). It does not mention the Denied Petitions List.

fact_check.claim: Courses on the Denied Petitions List cannot be petitioned again
fact_check.note: Petitions page: courses already petitioned and approved or denied are not accepted again; check the Denied list first.

fact_check.claim: Duffield students can petition unlisted, not-already-denied courses, but the page recommends listed courses first
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Courses from CALS, A&S, AAP and AEM must be under 3 credits; petitions for 3+ credits from those colleges not accepted
fact_check.note: Rule is right, but the page makes exceptions the article omits: A&S foreign language courses and some graduate courses are reviewed case by case. The 'Common mistakes' bullet 'Taking a 3-credit A&S course and petitioning it. Those are not accepted' is therefore too absolute.

fact_check.claim: Courses from Human Ecology, Brooks School of Public Policy and Nolan School of Hotel Administration are not accepted
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: The petitions page states no petition deadline
fact_check.note: No deadline stated; page says check with Duffield advising.

fact_check.claim: Engineering caps students at 20 credits a semester
fact_check.note: The Sun (March 31, 2022) says the college allows at most 20 credits per semester, down from 23. The article states it in the present tense as a current rule from a 2022 newspaper; a hard rule needs an official Cornell source or a dated statement.

fact_check.claim: One student told the Sun in 2022 that with the 18-credit requirement it was hard to fit outside electives
fact_check.note: Fair Shen '25 worried the policy could stop outside electives (wants an Asian religion class, 'just can't now'). Paraphrase is fair and attributed. Note the Sun mentions the 18 credits of liberal arts for engineering generally, not the Fall 2024 rule.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential thread 'Credit-Filler Courses' dates from July 2008
fact_check.note: Started July 2, 2008.

fact_check.claim: Brown_man1987 called Psych 101 reputedly one of the easiest classes
fact_check.note: Posted July 3, matches.

fact_check.claim: Brown_man1987 said the 'departmental sociology intro' had a median of A
fact_check.note: Brown_man1987 recommended DSoc 101 (Development Sociology) over Soc 101 because its median grade is an A. 'Departmental sociology intro' misidentifies the course; Spanks separately suggested Sociology 101.

fact_check.claim: cuapplecider9 said mushroom/fungi and dinosaur classes are considered easy, and Space Exploration was hard without astronomy background, five papers and a C
fact_check.note: Matches the post of July 2, 2008.

fact_check.claim: Brown_man1987 said uncurved courses are often the easy-A ones, curved courses often set the mean at B or B-
fact_check.note: Thread says many easy-A classes are uncurved and many science, math and engineering courses are curved to a B or B-. 'Set the mean' is a slight shift from the source wording (another poster, Biophilic, discusses median vs mean); reword to match.

fact_check.claim: dewdrop87 warned median grades would appear on transcripts, so a poor grade in a high-median course could look bad
fact_check.note: Post says medians posted on transcripts for students entering Fall 2008 and later; this is a 2008 policy statement and the article does not say whether it still applies today.

fact_check.claim: 'you have 8 semesters' for a first-year
fact_check.note: No source link; low-stakes but it is a hard-looking number with no citation.

beats_top.query: cornell engineering liberal studies easy courses
beats_top.why: The #1 result is an auto-generated spam page (it would not load for me, ECONNREFUSED, and search described it as unreliable), so the real competitor is Engineering's official liberal studies page, which owns the rules. Our page matches it on the rules but, to a student wanting easy picks, the first paragraph delivers no pick and no direct path to the approved list; the only course names are from a 2008 thread.
changes: Open with a direct answer: no official difficulty data exists, so find candidates in the official approved list filtered by category and check each course's syllabus and past median grades, with direct links to the approved list and denied list.

Link the official lists directly (liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu/approved, /denied, and engineering.cornell.edu/apps/liberalstudies) instead of routing every link through the Duffield overview page.
Make the 2008 anecdotes clearly secondary and accurate; add an 'if you are a first-year' step list that is sourced.

fixes: In 'What students say', change the first Brown_man1987 bullet so it says he said Psych 101 is reputedly one of the easiest classes and recommended DSoc 101 over Soc 101 because its median grade is an A; do not write 'departmental sociology intro'. Source https://talk.collegeconfidential.com/t/credit-filler-courses/520677 (July 2008).

Reword the uncurved/curved bullet to match the thread: Brown_man1987 said many easy-A classes are uncurved, while many science, math and engineering courses are curved to a B or B-. Drop 'set the mean'.
In the dewdrop87 bullet add that the transcript-median remark was about students entering in Fall 2008 and later and that the article has not verified whether it still applies.

In step 6 of 'How to pick a lighter course', change 'Engineering caps students at 20 credits a semester' to a dated statement: 'The Sun reported in March 2022 that Engineering limited students to 20 credits per semester (down from 23); confirm the current limit with Duffield Engineering Advising', or replace it with an official Cornell source for the current cap.

In 'Petitions, and where they trap people' and in 'Common mistakes', add the exception from https://liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu/petitions: A&S foreign language courses and some graduate courses are reviewed case by case; change the bullet 'Taking a 3-credit A&S course and petitioning it. Those are not accepted.' to say 3-credit-or-more A&S courses are not accepted except foreign language courses (reviewed case by case).

Add direct links to https://liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu/approved and https://liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu/denied in step 1 and step 2 and in the FAQ 'Where is the approved list?' answer (currently all three point to the Duffield overview page).

Remove 'you have 8 semesters' from the first-year bullet or replace it with sourced wording; rewrite the opening paragraph so it states the answer first: no official or current list of easy courses exists; use the approved list by category, compare syllabi and workload, and see below for the rules, with the 2008 thread only as dated anecdote.
